title: Earlier Declined Limit Reviews and Requests for Information: Personal Sender Account Review Timing
content:
When a limit review request is lodged on a Personal Sender Account, earlier declined decisions are read from the account history over the 24 months before the request date, an entry dated on the same calendar day 24 months earlier or before it no longer counting. When the history shows at least 1 limit review decision with the outcome declined and at least 1 request for information issued in those 24 months, 2 business days are added to the counted decision window of the request. When it shows a declined decision but no request for information in those 24 months, 1 business day is added to the counted decision window. When it shows no declined decision in those 24 months, nothing is added for earlier decisions.

## Combinations

| Declined limit review decisions in the 24 months | Requests for information issued in the 24 months | Business days added |
|---|---|---|
| 1 or more | 1 or more | 2 |
| 1 or more | none | 1 |
| none | 1 or more | 0 |
| none | none | 0 |

## Questions this rule answers

**Which entries count as a declined decision?** A limit review decision recorded on the account history with the outcome declined. A decision with the outcome approved or more information needed is not a declined decision.

**Which requests for information count?** Every request for information issued on the account and dated inside the 24 months, whatever its topic.

**Does a second declined decision add more?** No. The tiers turn on at least 1 declined decision; two or more declined decisions with a request for information still add 2 business days.

**Where does the 24-month window start?** Hypothetical dates: for a request lodged on 10 June of a given year, an entry dated 11 June two years earlier still counts, and an entry dated 10 June two years earlier, or before it, no longer counts.

**Does a request for information alone add anything?** No. Without a declined decision in the 24 months nothing is added for earlier decisions, whatever the number of requests for information.
